judgment.reasoning_summary: The problem requires finding the smallest integer k such that in any n x n grid, there exists at least one good rectangle if n >= k. A good rectangle is defined as a rectangle formed by four squares with the property that the four corner squares are the same color. The solution involves combinatorial arguments and the pigeonhole principle to ensure that for sufficiently large n, there will always be at least one good rectangle.
